No, we can create a QR code before the website is published. The important thing is deciding where the QR code will direct visitors.

There are two options:

Option 1 — Publish the website first (recommended)

We publish HyTwin Discovery Lab using GitHub Pages, obtain its public URL, and generate a QR code linking directly to it.

Option 2 — Create the QR code now

We can choose the intended website address, such as:

https://shakilabibi1.github.io/hytwin-discovery-lab/

Then generate the QR code immediately and place it on your PowerPoint poster.

The QR code will scan, but the website won't open successfully until it's published at that address.

What I recommend

Since your GitHub repository is already created, we can generate the QR code now using the planned GitHub Pages address.

We can continue editing the website afterwards without changing the QR code, provided its URL stays the same.

This means we can finish the poster while continuing to improve the website.

One consideration: GitHub Pages availability for private repositories depends on your GitHub plan. We may eventually need to make the website repository public or use another hosting arrangement.

Would you like me to generate the QR code now using your planned GitHub Pages address?
